title: Design, synthesis, and antiseizure evaluation of benzhydryl 5-arylfuran-2-carboxylates: GABA-A/SV2A targeting, EEG, and ADMET profiling
content: Epilepsy is a persistent neurological disorder marked by recurrent, unprovoked seizures and remains a major worldwide healthcare challenge owing to its profound clinical, cognitive, and psychosocial consequences. This research aimed to design and synthesize a novel series of benzhydryl 5-arylfuran-2-carboxylates via Suzuki cross-coupling (5a–5i), affording good to excellent yields (74–96%), and to evaluate antiseizure potential using acute PTZ-induced seizure and 6 Hz psychomotor seizure models. The 3, 5d, 5e, and 5f showed anticonvulsant potential, with notable improvements in mortality, seizure protection, and severity. Further, docking studies against the GABA-A receptor gave scores of −7.318 to −8.594 kcal mol−1, all more favourable than diazepam and levetiracetam, with 5i, 5e and 5c showing the most favourable predicted docking scores. At human SV2A (PDB: 9OKG), scores ranged from −5.498 to −8.048 kcal mol−1, and only 3 and 5f scored better than diazepam and levetiracetam. Compound 5d showed a favourable GABA-A score (−8.126) but a weak SV2A score (−5.854), suggesting that its activity is more consistent with GABA-A than SV2A. Predicted permeability was accompanied by low aqueous solubility and potential toxicity liabilities. Network pharmacology identified 17 candidate genes common to all ten compounds and epilepsy, including PTGS2, ALOX5, GSK3β, and HDAC4/6, which may suggest involvement of neuroinflammatory, eicosanoid, and epigenetic pathways; these are computational predictions that were not validated experimentally. Overall, compound 5d was the most promising candidate from the in vivo data for further preclinical investigation and anticonvulsant agent development.
